snapshot.how: compute.py and counts.cpp copied unchanged to a build directory outside manuscript/ (a temporary directory unless --build-dir is given) and run there via compute.main(); counts.cpp compiled locally with clang++ -O3 -std=c++17; the snapshot's own outputs (results.json, report.md, run_*.json) stay in that directory
validation: NTT modulus 3221225473 verified prime by trial division; primitive root 5 verified using both prime factors 2 and 3 of modulus-1.
Exact rational g/(6/pi^2) agrees with independent brute local-residue densities for all 1275 pairs q<=50; finite Euler product over primes<=50 divided out exactly.
Brute squarefree frequencies at x=1000000, q<=50: maximum absolute density discrepancy 3.17040894156e-05.
sum_l Q(x;q,l)=Q(x;1,1) exactly for every q<=50 at x=1000000 (Q=607926).
At x=257 every generated modulus for all three polynomials: exact sum Q^2 and both rational density coefficients agree with direct residue counts.

Every production x: NTT autocorrelation C(0) and seven direct lag sums checked with exact integers. NTT prime 3221225473 (primitive root 5, up to length 2^30) exceeds every autocorrelation coefficient; no modular ambiguity.

precision.snapshot_V: decimal arithmetic with decimal.getcontext().prec = 70 (set by the snapshot compute.py); the integer counts are exact
precision.mpmath_dps_note: set globally by the snapshot compute.py when it is imported; reproduce.py sets no precision of its own. Used for the comparison of V with the archive and for the values of zeta(2), zeta(3), zeta(-1/2) and Euler gamma, which are then rounded to double precision
precision.theory_constants: IEEE double precision (numpy float64, math.fsum) for R_f, B_f, H_f(-1/2), K_f, W_f, Theta_f, F_f and Vaughan c_2; rounding is not certified

vaughan_c2.note: c_2 from Vaughan (2005), (1.14)-(1.15) with k=2, Euler product truncated at the same cutoff

fixed_ratio.aggregation: Mean of eight ratio-specific log-log slopes; SE is across-ratio SE. Individual regression SEs below.

uncertainty_note: Extrapolation uncertainties are the snapshot heuristic sensitivity envelope, not confidence intervals. The standard errors of the fixed-x and joint regressions are formal OLS values; the fixed-ratio standard error is the standard error of the mean of the eight ratio-specific slopes (sample standard deviation divided by sqrt(8)), not an OLS regression standard error. None of these is a rigorous error bound. The K_f truncation bound is rigorous for the omitted primes but floating-point rounding is not certified.
